`Refunder.refund` in `src/refunds.ts` exists to satisfy three requirements. I got this from `ostf context src/refunds.ts#Refunder.refund`, and I changed no files.

**Why it exists**
- **R-REFUND-LIMIT:** A refund must not exceed what is left of the original charge. Refunds above 500.00 in one UTC day for an account need a second approval.
  - This item is marked **risk-relevant**, so you should be asked before it is changed.
  - It controls RISK-REFUND-ABUSE, where a compromised account or a mistaken operator drains funds through refunds.
  - It refines N-REFUNDS, which says customers get refunds quickly without the business losing money to abuse.
  - It is also implemented by `checkRefundLimit` in `src/refunds.ts`.
- **R-AUDIT-MONEY:** Every charge and every refund appends an audit entry with the time, account, action, amount and receipt.
  - It refines N-ACCOUNT-SAFE.
  - Its other implementer is `Processor.charge` in `src/payments.ts`.
- **R-REFUND-ORIGINAL:** A refund goes back to the payment method of the charge it refunds, never to another one.
  - It refines N-REFUNDS.
  - It is also implemented by `Gateway` and `Processor.receipt` in `src/payments.ts`.

**Tests that cover it**
- `src/refunds.test.ts#Refunder > totals refunds per account and UTC day` verifies R-REFUND-LIMIT.
- `src/refunds.test.ts#checkRefundLimit` verifies R-REFUND-LIMIT.
- `src/refunds.test.ts#Refunder > refunds to the original transaction` verifies both R-AUDIT-MONEY and R-REFUND-ORIGINAL.
- `src/payments.test.ts#Processor > appends an audit entry` verifies R-AUDIT-MONEY. It tests the audit side through `Processor`, not `Refunder` directly.

All of these links are reported as valid.
